localBiteReport: The week of September 4–8, 2026, guides and local reporters covering Choctawhatchee Bay are noting the first clear signs of the fall transition: water temperatures beginning to edge down, large concentrations of baitfish moving out of open water and into bayous, bridge areas, and shallow flats. Redfish are showing up in improving numbers for sight-fishing opportunities on the flats, and the mullet migration — which typically pulls slot and bull reds into the bay in force — is expected to kick off in earnest during the second or third week of September. Bait schools (greenies/finger mullet) are now the key to finding fish; redfish are following them hard, and cut or butterfly-rigged finger mullet on a single-drop rig is the anticipated top presentation once that push arrives. Water temperature as of today (September 8) is 87°F. No specific speckled trout, flounder, sheepshead, or black drum catch numbers for the bay were reported this week, though conditions are trending in a favorable direction for all inshore species as late-summer heat slowly breaks.
